associations.rationale: The type gives only the cardinality of the opaque ComplementaryIndex type, not a family of representatives or the Frobenius-orbit isomorphism classification.
This is the pairwise-nonisomorphism condition for an already defined complementary family, so it supplies one component rather than the full stated classification.
The formal type establishes simplicity of each member of a predefined family, a constituent property rather than the source's orbit-and-representative assertion.
The iff directly characterizes isomorphism of complementary-series representations by equality up to complementaryCharFrobenius, i.e. the stated Frobenius-orbit classification.
The existential type directly provides a simple, pairwise-nonisomorphic family with cardinality q(q−1)/2, matching the representative-family portion of the source claim.
